after.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1-(-1)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

Question 3

The vector v in the plane is mapped to the vector [1−2] under the action of the linear transformation T whose matrix T is given by T=[2513]. What is the original vector v?

a
[3−15]
b
[−23]
c
[3−5]
d
[1−5]
e
[13−5]
Submit

decision.explanation: Writing v=(x,y), we need 2x+5y=1 and x+3y=-2. Subtracting twice the second equation from the first gives -y=5, so y=-5 and x=13. Check: 2(13)+5(-5)=1 and 13+3(-5)=-2.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
after.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6-5}[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$

after.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{15-12}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}21 \\ -27\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
